method: In-tree build script reproduces the deployed stripped binary byte for byte; configure arguments, dynamic metadata and on-board transfers reviewed

details.configure_arguments: --host=arm-uclinuxfdpiceabi --prefix=/usr --enable-static --disable-shared --enable-ipv6 --disable-threaded-resolver --with-mbedtls=<staged Mbed TLS> --with-default-ssl-backend=mbedtls --with-ca-bundle=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt; all other TLS backends and the compression, HTTP/2, IDN, LDAP, SSH and mail/file-transfer protocol backends disabled
details.reproduction: make curl run twice from the published script; rootfs/usr/bin/curl identical both times (sha256 487f1a46..., 465364 bytes stripped)
details.size: Built -Os with -ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections and -Wl,--gc-sections: the text segment is 446444 bytes, so the no-MMU loader's single contiguous mapping for it fits an order-7 (512 KiB) buddy block. The default -O2 build produced a 552960-byte segment that needed order-8, and once those were gone the loader failed with 'nommu: Allocation of length 552960 from process N (curl) failed' and the program died; observed on hardware after the board had been up a while, gone from the shipped build.
details.linked_libraries: libmbedtls.so.21, libmbedx509.so.7, libmbedcrypto.so.16, libc.so.0 (FDPIC shared objects; no TEXTREL, e_flags 0x05000400 hard-float matches rootfs libgcc_s.so.1)
details.protocols: file ftp ftps http https ipfs ipns ws wss
details.features: alt-svc HSTS HTTPS-proxy IPv6 Largefile SSL threadsafe UnixSockets
details.on_board: Verified on the N32H787 board with the shipped rootfs: https://example.com/ and https://curl.se/ return 200 with certificate verification enabled, a self-signed host is rejected, and a 38 MB https download of a mirror index completes intact
details.licenses: curl license (MIT/X derivative); COPYING preserved in licenses/curl/COPYING and installed in the rootfs
details.xattr: Rebuilt after the toolchain sysroot restored the xattr interface (UCLIBC_HAS_XATTR): the binary now carries curl's fsetxattr path. On the board, --xattr on a filesystem without xattr support prints "Operation not supported", still saves the file and exits 0.
